therapeutic_hypothesis.target_population: Patients with probable Alzheimer's disease and healthy volunteers
therapeutic_hypothesis.primary_endpoint: Sensitivity and specificity of florbetaben PET scans using two separate algorithms (BAPL scoring) with onsite clinical diagnosis as standard of truth

results.effect_size: Sensitivity 67.24–79.49%; Specificity 89.18–96.61% across algorithms and parts
results.target_engagement_evidence: SUVR in AD patients consistently higher than HV across all cortical regions (e.g., composite SUVR AD Part B: 1.678 vs HV Part B: 1.355)
biomarker_changes: Composite SUVR AD Part A: 1.620 vs HV Part A: 1.320
Composite SUVR AD Part B: 1.678 vs HV Part B: 1.355
Frontal cortex SUVR AD Part B: 1.646 vs HV Part B: 1.301
Posterior cingulate SUVR AD Part B: 1.852 vs HV Part B: 1.493
Anterior cingulate SUVR AD Part B: 1.786 vs HV Part B: 1.434
Kappa inter-reader agreement at 90-110 min Part B: 0.86
subgroup_findings: 45-60 min window Part A: Sensitivity 73.93%, Specificity 94.61%
110-130 min window Part A: Sensitivity 70.56%, Specificity 98.01%
safety_signals: Arrhythmia in 1 AD patient (Part A) and 1 healthy volunteer (Part B)
Chest pain in 1 AD patient (Part A)
Clear cell endometrial carcinoma in 1 healthy volunteer (Part B)

context.duration: Single imaging session; study ran August 2008 to November 2010
